note: Runtime V4 world-delta vocabulary (docs/RUNTIME_V4_PLAN.md §5). One source for the extractor prompt, its schema and the validator (src/v4/extract.js); the domain/authority firewall (src/v4/firewall.js) decides what of a schema-valid answer the engine commits. D2 = A (P0/S2): the narrator writes prose only, the extractor reads each reply afterwards. delta-0.2 against the P0 draft delta-0.1-draft: expected of a pending buy/pay also asks taken_anyway (P0/S2 v12_08: the reply had Alaric take the room unasked, the free overreach delta was missed, the expected fields were 25/25); position, aware, intent and thread as in 3.x; creature.new and person.new carry the distance band a fight needs; check without the numbers the prose does not show. delta-0.3 (product 4.0): expected of a sell asks sold and price_cp (the world applier books a sale by them; before, a sell fell back to {done} and could never be booked); no delta type changed. delta-0.4 (live run 28.09.2026): the extractor also reads the PLAYER MESSAGE; what it has Alaric say or do himself ("*i sign the card*") is never overreach, a payment, purchase, acceptance, registration or journey that PLAYER ACTIONS did not book still is; a name Alaric gives is learned by those who hear it; no delta type changed. delta-0.5 (live run 28.09.2026 afternoon): name learning requires diegetic transmission; deltas caused only by an overreaching Alaric action are omitted; no delta type changed. delta-0.6 (live run 28.09.2026 15:17): an engine-resolved SEARCH CHECK is never re-reported as a check; tracks/signs of an unseen unknown creature are evidence, not creature.new; Guild quest.detail may add operational fiction but never payout/proof/completion/rank mechanics; no delta type changed. delta-0.7: explicit null names stay anonymous; booked objects are not recreated; extractor gets Core Range Band semantics. delta-0.8: visible fantasy creatures carry a separate mechanical F1 body-plan anchor so creative species names never fail entity creation; a revealed creature is immediately profile-locked for target/HP display. Quest gather yields: concrete gathered amounts for an active Guild GATHER objective become canonical quest resource objects, so later proof checks use real inventory rather than a progress-only fact. delta-0.9 soft-world simplification: ordinary NPC/world causality is stored rather than pre-authorized; NPC->PC hand-overs are allowed; Guild proof is guidance, while quest.ready records that the desired story outcome has been achieved before deterministic turn-in/payout/XP. delta-0.10 boundary cleanup: remove obsolete generic check deltas, allow explicit externally-forced relocation, keep soft persistence tolerant while Combat/progression remain strict. delta-0.11: preserve first-read Board availability and treat ambient herds as grouped background rather than Combat entities. delta-0.12 (integration of 30.09.2026): companions and names keep one identity across scene changes — arrive.with (and with in an expected go answer) lists who arrives together with Alaric, everyone else stays behind; person.named gives a person known without a name the name the story now says, instead of a second person.new. A group is always reported as creature.new with its count: whether a large passive group of skittish animals is background (one fact) or individual combatants is the engine's decision (src/v4/world.js), not the extractor's. Coin is a number, never an object: loose coin in object.new is refused, coin Alaric gains (a gift, loot, a found purse's contents) is coin.gift; the Guild's payout and coin the engine already booked are never coin.gift. An unpriced buy stays an open decision until the player agrees: the expected buy/pay answer counts consent the reply invents for Alaric ("at his nod") and service, consumption or payment before his own agreement as taken_anyway (live 30.09.2026: water poured, paid and drunk before a price was agreed). The overreach rule keeps the two clauses of delta-0.4 that the soft-overreach rewrite of delta-0.9 had dropped (live 28.09.2026): the PLAYER MESSAGE's own words and gestures are never overreach, and a commitment PLAYER ACTIONS did not book stays overreach even when the player wrote it. delta-0.13 (review of 4.1.0): an offer line is a lot, qty units for price_cp together (a price per piece is qty 1); coin.gift names in from the person who hands it over, or where Alaric takes it from (the engine books coin nobody hands him only after his own TAKE, and never twice); quest.offer is work someone asks Alaric to do for them: someone offering to guide, accompany or help him is a fact or an intent, not a quest. delta-0.14 (live run 30.09.2026 14:56): quest.ready carries alternative: when fewer targets of a DEFEAT objective were defeated than it names (the engine counts the kills), how the story reached the outcome otherwise, else null; trophies are no count. Only the listed delta types exist: a new place comes into being through the place ref of an arrive (or of person.new at), never a delta of its own (the run's extractor twice sent type "place"). The natural steps of an action PLAYER ACTIONS booked (registering: signing, the measuring stone, back to the counter) are part of it, never overreach. delta-0.15 (live run 30.09.2026 22:41): creature.new carries stronger: true when the reply clearly establishes the individual as bigger or stronger than ordinary ones of its kind; the engine then gives it the individual variation of Content #7 (its numbers, and by them its Defeat XP); a name alone, anger or drama is no such evidence, and Elite/Boss are never inferred. A Guild contract's quest.detail keeps the story; its status, payout, XP and rank are the engine's (the run stored "Contract registered and active; payout 60 cp" while the contract was still on the board).
rules: Report only what THIS reply establishes, in the order it happens (seq 1, 2, 3 …). Invent nothing.
Alaric's own decisions are in PLAYER ACTIONS and already booked by the engine; never report them as deltas (no payment, purchase, acceptance, turn-in, pick-up of his).

Overreach is only for meaningful voluntary PC commitments the narrator invented: paying/buying, accepting/turning in/registering, setting off for a new destination, attacking, giving away/dropping his property, or Alaric himself picking up/taking something he had not chosen to take. Ordinary world causality is not overreach: NPCs may give Alaric items, help him, refuse him, accompany him, leave, reveal information, create witnesses or otherwise act for their own reasons. Record those world changes normally. What the PLAYER MESSAGE has him say or do himself (his words, a gesture, signing, sitting down) is his own, never overreach; but coin, goods, contracts, registration and journeys change only as PLAYER ACTIONS book them: a payment, purchase, pick-up, acceptance, turn-in, registration or journey that the reply shows, that PLAYER ACTIONS do not book and the CATALOG does not show as done already, is overreach, even when the PLAYER MESSAGE has him do it. The natural steps of an action PLAYER ACTIONS booked are part of that action, never overreach: registering includes signing, the measuring stone and coming back to the counter; a purchase includes carrying it off; a journey includes the road.
Answer every key of expected; each key asks about the PLAYER ACTION with the same number.
Known places, people, quests and objects by their id from the CATALOG; a new place as {"new": {"name", "kind", "parent"}} (parent: a place id or one more {"new": …}).

Prices and coin are integers in copper (1 silver = 10 copper, 1 gold = 100 copper). The Guild's contract payout and its registration fee are the engine's; report the story's words about them only as facts.
Official Guild contracts come only from the engine's BOARD; never report a new one (if the reply shows one the BOARD lacks: overreach guild_listing).

During the reply that FIRST SHOWS the just-generated official BOARD, every listed quest is still available. Do not claim it was already taken or emit listing.gone in that SAME reading reply. Later, causally established world changes may remove an ignored listing.
A price someone merely mentions is a fact; an offer is a price for something Alaric could buy now.

A person learns Alaric's name only from diegetic evidence: Alaric explicitly says it where they hear him, or visibly writes/shows it where the reply establishes they read it. Third-person narration merely calling the protagonist "Alaric" or "Alaric Red" is never evidence that an NPC learned his name.

Tracks, spoor, hair, a wallow, sounds, shadows or other evidence of an unseen/unknown creature are evidence, not creature.new. Report the evidence as a fact or thread. Use creature.new only when the reply establishes the creature itself as an actual individual/group; keep its in-world species name and choose the separate nearest mechanical anchor.

For a known Guild contract, quest.detail may freely store operational story information such as contacts, routes, witnesses, schedules, discovered requirements or plausible verification. It may never alter or restate the engine-owned payout, Guild rank, Quest XP, formal status (registered, active, completed, turned in) or promotion mechanics: those clauses are dropped.

Range Bands use Core #12 only: ENGAGED = immediate contact/melee reach; SHORT = one normal combat movement from ENGAGED; MEDIUM = two; LONG = three. Convert an exact narrated distance once to the most reasonable band. A person about forty yards ahead is not ENGAGED. Preserve an established band unless the reply clearly changes distance; threat/intensity alone never changes a band.
When PLAYER ACTIONS already grant or create a Guild plate, contract slip or other object, do not emit object.new for the narrated hand-over or description of that same booked object.

For person.new, name:null means the reply did not establish a proper name. Never infer a proper name from the ref token, a nearby place/business title, or capitalization; keep the person anonymous until the story actually names them. When the story later names such a known person, report person.named {who: their id, name}, never a second person.new for them.

For creature.new, species is the creature's actual in-world name/type from the reply and may be newly invented fantasy fauna. Separately choose anchor as the nearest ecological/mechanical F1 body-plan from the allowed anchor enum. Do not force the creative species name to equal an anchor. Example: a low plated badger-lizard-like wallow beast may be species:"plated wallow beast", anchor:"armored_beast".

creature.new stronger: true only when the reply clearly establishes this individual (or each of the group) as bigger or stronger than ordinary ones of its kind (half again the size of the others, the heaviest bull of the herd); the engine then fixes its stronger numbers once. Never from a name or label alone ("big boar" said in passing), never for anger, wounds or drama; otherwise null. Elite and Boss are never inferred.

When creatures become visible in the scene, report creature.new immediately (one entry per kind of creature, count for a group), so their canonical target handles, HP and Range are locked before the player chooses to attack. The engine keeps a large passive flock or herd as one background fact; an animal the story later singles out, threatens or attacks is a creature.new of its own.

When PLAYER ACTIONS contains a GATHERS activity and the reply establishes a concrete amount actually gathered for an active Quest GATHER objective, emit object.new for the amount gained THIS reply: kind:"resource", holder:"pc", for_quest:<that quest id>, name matching the objective/proof resource, qty the amount gained, unit matching the objective/proof. A progress fact alone is not enough. Do not emit resources the reply did not say were gathered.

Guild contract proof/verification is narrative guidance, not an exact inventory-string gate. Store the expected verification so the narrator remembers what the job is about, but alternative credible in-world evidence may satisfy the fiction.

For every active Guild contract in the CATALOG, compare THIS reply with its desired end state before answering. When THIS reply clearly establishes that desired end state as substantively achieved, you MUST emit quest.ready even if you also emit arrive, fact, quest.progress or memory; do not leave a clearly achieved contract outcome only as a fact or memory. Partial progress, merely finding a clue, traveling to the site, or planning the next step is not enough. quest.ready does not complete or pay the quest; the player must still explicitly turn it in at a Guild hall.

A known object voluntarily handed to Alaric by an NPC is object.move to:"pc", even if Alaric only asked for it and did not issue a TAKE command. For a newly introduced gift, emit object.new with the giver/NPC as holder and then object.move to:"pc". These are NPC/world agency, not overreach. An unattended object lying in the world still requires Alaric's own TAKE if he picks it up.

arrive.forced_by is only for an external event that actually relocates Alaric against or independently of his voluntary travel choice (for example arrest, being carried, a collapsing floor, abduction). Do not use it to invent ordinary voluntary travel.

When Alaric arrives somewhere together with people (a client he escorts, a driver, a guide, companions), list their ids from PRESENT in arrive.with, or in the with of the expected go answer. Whoever is not listed stayed behind at the old place.
Soft continuity deltas are memory, not mechanics. Prefer recording the durable fact once over splitting ordinary fiction into several redundant deltas.
Only the delta types listed below exist. A new place comes into being only through the place ref of an arrive (or the at of a person.new) as {"new": …}; there is no delta for a place alone.

go.summary: did he arrive, where, and who came with him

shape.with: ids of the people who arrived with him, or null

activity.summary: how long it took, and whether he finished

buy.summary: did someone name a price; did the reply show Alaric take, use, consume or pay for it before he himself agreed to that price (a nod or consent the reply invents for him is no agreement)

pay.summary: did someone name the amount; did the reply show Alaric pay before he himself agreed to it (a nod or consent the reply invents for him is no agreement)

sell.summary: did a buyer take it and pay, and how much

deltas.summary: story time that passed

Alaric arrives somewhere after his own GO/roaming action, or because the reply explicitly establishes an external involuntary cause in forced_by; with: the ids of the people who travel and arrive together with him (null when he arrives without anyone)
a person the reply introduces; name only a proper name, else null; present: here with Alaric now; at: where they are if not here
the reply says the proper name of a person already known (in PRESENT or the CATALOG) who had no name so far

creatures the reply itself establishes as actual creatures; species is the in-world/display species name, anchor is the nearest F1 mechanical body-plan; never tracks/spoor/hair/sounds alone; count > 1 makes separate creatures; band is current distance; stronger: true only when the reply clearly establishes this individual as bigger or stronger than ordinary ones of its kind (never a name alone), else null
a known person comes into the scene
a person leaves or stays behind
a lasting world fact (not about what Alaric holds, pays or has decided)
what a person now knows
a real change in how someone regards Alaric
a moment people will remember

a physical thing the reply establishes; for a new NPC gift create it with the NPC as holder, then object.move it to "pc"; Alaric directly holds a newly introduced object only after his TAKE/GATHER; loose coin is never an object (coin Alaric gains is coin.gift)
someone/something moves a known object; NPC -> Alaric is allowed as ordinary world agency; never move Alaric's property away from him unless his own action or coercion authorizes it
an object gets a mark ("signed by the waystation master")

someone names prices; lines: what, kind (goods|service), service (lodging, bath, laundry, meal, healing, training, other or null), qty: how many units the price is for (1 for a price per piece, 3 for "three for nine copper"), price_cp: the price of those qty units together

Alaric receives coin: someone gives it to him of their own will, or he takes coin that is really there (loot, the contents of a found purse); from: the person who hands it over, or where he takes it from ("the bandit's purse"); never the Guild's payout and never coin the engine already booked
something is taken from Alaric against his will (never by the other side of a sale)
private work someone asks Alaric to do for them (never a Guild contract); someone offering to guide, accompany or help Alaric is a fact or an intent, not a quest
persistent quest/world information for narration: contacts, routes, witnesses, schedules, discovered facts or plausible verification; never changes engine payout/rank/XP/completed status
an objective visibly advanced (information only)

the reply clearly establishes that an active quest's desired story outcome has been substantively achieved; memory/readiness only, not completion, payout or XP; alternative: when fewer targets were defeated than a DEFEAT objective names (see its engine count), how the story reached the outcome otherwise ("the last strider fled the flats for good"), else null; trophies or a claimed number are no count
private work closed by its giver; a Guild contract only as failed (it became impossible): Guild contracts are completed only when Alaric turns them in at a Guild hall
a board listing is taken by someone else or withdrawn
who commits to attack Alaric right now
where someone present now stands relative to Alaric (outside a fight)
whether someone present has noticed Alaric
what someone hostile means to do on their next turn
a story thread that will matter again (a threat, a promise, a debt), or one that is resolved now
rest or healing outside combat
the narrator invented a meaningful voluntary PC commitment that the player did not choose (protected mechanics/agency only, not normal NPC/world causality)
